sentences.text: Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.125 of 2017
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard Smt. D.Madhavi, learned Standing Counsel for HMDA, appearing for the appellant and Sri Alladi Ravinder, learned counsel,
representing Sri Mettapalli Srininvas, learned counsel on record for the respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act'), is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer, HMDA, Begumpet, Hyderabad, aggrieved by the order and decree dated 31.12.2013 passed in L.A.O.P.No.310 of 2006 on the file of the VII Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar (hereinafter referred to as 'the Reference Court'), whereby the compensation for the subject lands acquired in Shivarampally Village, Rajendernagar Manal, was enhanced from Rs.4,60,000/- per acre to Rs.500/-per square yard.
2
AKS,J & LNA, J 3.

The undisputed facts of the case are that an extent of Acs.10.22  guntas of land situated in Shivarampally Village, Rajendernagar Mandal, which includes the lands belonging to respondents/claimants, was acquired for the purpose of construction of Sewerage Treatment Plant at Mir-Alam Tank; that draft Notification under Section-4(1) of the Act was published on 22.09.2003; that during survey and sub-division, the area in Sy.No.5 has been increased from Acs.7.19 guntas to Acs.7.2  guntas and the amendment was made to the draft notification in respect of Sy.No.5/4; that the same was published in A.P. Gazette on 08.03.2004; that draft declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published in District Gazette on 09.03.2004; and that the Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting necessary award enquiry, passed an Award dated 23.01.2006, fixing the market value of the acquired lands @ Rs.4,60,000/- per acre and granted other benefits to the respondents/claimants.
4. Not being satisfied with the said Award, the respondents/claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act 3 AKS,J & LNA, J and the same was numbered as L.A.O.P.No.310 of 2006 on the file of the Reference Court.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Officer vs P. Venkat Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondent/claimant, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-9 were marked.
On behalf of the appellant-Referring Officer, R.W-1 was examined and Ex.B-1-Award dated 21.01.2006 was marked.

6. It is contended by the learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant that the Reference Court has erred in relying upon Exs.A-1, A-8 and A-9-sale deeds as the same pertain to house sites, whereas the acquired lands of the respondents/claimants are agricultural lands and not part of any sanctioned lay out and therefore, the Reference Court erred in fixing the market value of the acquired lands on yardage basis.
Learned Government Pleader, therefore, prayed to set aside the impugned order.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants contended that the Reference Court taking into consideration the exhibits, particularly Exs.A-1, A-8 and A-9, enhanced the market 4 AKS,J & LNA, J value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer duly assigning reasons therefor and as such, the impugned order needs no interference by this Court and the Appeal is liable to be dismissed.

8. Before the Reference Court, the respondents/claimants have marked as many as nine exhibits,
i.e., Exs.A-1 to A-9 and they particularly relied upon Exs.A-1 and A-9 in support of their claim for enhancement of compensation in respect of the acquired lands.

Ex.A-1 is the sale deed whereunder Dharani Co-Operative Society Limited purchased property and the proceedings issued by District Registrar impounding the document in the year 2001 shows that the basic value of the land is Rs.400/- per square yard and accordingly, the stamp duty was collected @ Rs.400/- per square yard in the year 1997.

Ex.A-9 is the sale deed bearing document No.588/2002 dated 04.02.2002,
whereunder the plot situated in Sy.No.14 of Shivarampally Village, admeasuring 90 square yards,
was purchased for a consideration of Rs.45,000/-.

By relying on the said two documents, the respondents/claimants contended that the lands covered under the said sale deeds are similar in nature and potentiality and are located in the vicinity of the acquired lands and 5 AKS,J & LNA, J hence, the same needs to be considered for fixing the market value of the acquired lands.

9. From a close scrutiny of the Award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, it is evident that the sale transactions that took place in respect of lands in Sy.Nos.2, 3 and 4 in the year 2000 and Sy.No.14/A/B/C in the year 2013, which admittedly are very adjacent to the acquired lands, are on yardage basis.
The Land Acquisition Officer failed to give proper reasons for discarding the said documents and calculating the market value of the acquired lands on acreage basis.

However, the Reference Court by observing that the lands situated in Sy.Nos.5, 12 and 13, which are adjacent to the acquired lands, were sold on yardage basis, found fault with the Award of the Land Acquisition Officer insofar as awarding compensation for the acquired lands on acreage basis.
This Court is of the opinion that the Reference Court, appreciating the evidence on record in a proper perspective,
rightly
calculated the market value of the acquired lands on acreage basis, which warrants no interference by this Court.

sentences.text: As regards the assessment of the market value of the acquired lands, it is to be seen that as per Ex.A-1-sale deed, which pertains to an extent of 179 square yards of land, the market value of the subject land therein works out to Rs.400/- per square yard and as per Ex.A-9-sale deed, the market value of the land therein works out to Rs. 500/- per square yard.

11. In this aspect, it is relevant to note the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Goa Housing Board Vs. Panduranga V.Sawanth1 and Atma Singh (died) through LRs. And others Vs. State of Haryana 2, wherein it is held that in the absence of any other evidence, the Court can take the documents under which small pieces of land were purchased into consideration for determining the value of the land.

entities.text: Goa Housing Board Vs. Panduranga V.Sawanth1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Atma Singh (died) through LRs. And others Vs. State of Haryana 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Though the extent covered by Ex.A-9 is very small, as the said transaction is genuine and relate to the land situated in the vicinity of the acquired lands, the sale price mentioned in the said document can be taken as comparative sale, as held by the Supreme 2010(15) SCC 276 2008(2) SCC 568 7 AKS,J & LNA, J Court in Goa Housing Board Vs. Panduranga V.Sawanth 3 and Atma Singh (died) through LRs.

entities.text: Goa Housing Board Vs. Panduranga V.Sawanth
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And others Vs. State of Haryana 4.
13.

entities.text: And others Vs. State of Haryana 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforesaid judgments, this Court is of the considered view that the Reference Court has rightly relied upon Exs.A-1 and A-8 and assessed the market value of the acquired lands @ Rs.500/- per square yard.

However, the Reference Court failed to take note of the fact that the acquired lands are not part of any lay out and are undeveloped, whereas the lands covered under Exs.A-1 and A-9 are situated in approved lay out,
and therefore, erred in not deducting amount towards developmental charges.

14. Hence, this Court feels it appropriate to deduct 35% of the market value of the acquired lands as assessed above, towards developmental charges, and thus, the respondents/claimants are entitled to Rs.325/- per square yard.

15. Accordingly, this Appeal is allowed in part, modifying the impugned order i.e., order dated 31.12.2013 passed in 2010(15) SCC 276 2008(2) SCC 568 8 AKS,J & LNA, J L.A.O.P.No.310 of 2006 on the file of the VII Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar to the extent indicated above and the market value of the subject acquired lands is fixed @ Rs.325/- per square yard.

entities.text: VII Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In all other respects, the impugned order remains unaltered.
16. As a sequel, interim order dated 13.03.2017 passed in LAASMP.No.225 of 2017 stands vacated.
Pending Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
No costs.
